---
title: "Social Security taxation reform"
subtitle: "Revenue and trust-fund effects of fifteen reforms, 2026-2100"
author:
  - "Max Ghenis"
  - "Ben Ogorek"
  - "Pavel Makarchuk"
  - "David Trimmer"
date: 2026-11-06
lang: en
abstract: |
  The Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget commissioned PolicyEngine to
  estimate how fifteen reforms to the taxation of Social Security benefits
  would change federal revenue and the Social Security and Medicare trust
  funds through 2100. We simulate each reform on PolicyEngine's populace
  microdata, which we project to 21 anchor years and calibrate to the 2026
  Trustees Reports' projections of current law, including the 2025
  reconciliation act.
  We estimate that repealing the tax on benefits would reduce federal revenue
  by $1.66 trillion over 2026-2035 and by $10.9 trillion in present value over
  75 years. Taxing all benefits would raise $896 billion over the first
  decade. Two Roth-style swaps would end the tax on benefits, one at once and
  one in phases, and tax workers on their employers' payroll contributions
  instead. They would raise revenue at first and lose it from the mid-2050s for
  the immediate swap and from 2060 for the phased one. From then on, the
  benefit-tax revenue they give up exceeds the income tax on employer
  contributions. We report every reform, year, and trust-fund split on the
  [interactive
  dashboard](https://policyengine.org/us/taxation-of-benefits-reforms).
keywords:
  - Social Security
  - Taxation of benefits
  - Trust funds
  - Microsimulation
  - PolicyEngine
  - CRFB
